featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

Excellent and tasty food is served here at Food Street, Mumbai, a popular destination for anyone who loves authentic Bombay flavors. This place brings together the city’s most famous street foods under one roof, offering a mix of taste, aroma, and tradition that Mumbai is known for. From the spicy kick of vada pav and the buttery goodness of pav bhaji to the tangy bhel puri and crispy sev puri, every dish reflects the city’s rich food culture.

The chefs here prepare each item with care, using fresh ingredients and maintaining the original Bombay taste that food lovers crave. Whether you prefer light snacks or filling meals, there’s something for everyone. The lively atmosphere, quick service, and friendly staff make dining here an enjoyable experience.

Food Street isn’t just a place to eat—it’s a celebration of Mumbai’s vibrant street food heritage. Locals come here to relive nostalgic flavors, while visitors get a true introduction to the city’s culinary charm. If you’re in Mumbai and looking for delicious, authentic, and affordable food, Food Street is the perfect stop to satisfy your hunger and enjoy Bombay’s famous taste in every bite.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is just outside the Charni road station East, you can see this place from the skywalk itself. On weekends you will find a really good young and family crowd at the same time you will experience a lot of people here. This place (The whole khau gali) only serves veg and you will get food in the price range of Rs. 40 to Rs. 200-250. It's a really nice place if you want to explore the food and don't want to be too harsh on your pocket as well. The place serves chaat, veg tikka, Franky, rolls, pasta, pizza, sandwiches, juice and shakes etc

The things which I tried and want you to experience are:

1. Paani Puri - So we started with chaat and we chose to try it from the shop so the puri which they served was of rawa so I will recommend you to try the chaat from the stall which is on the street and serves different types of paani.

2. Chinese bhel - This we tried from the street side stall but I felt this could have been better as I did not find that tangy taste and I have tried better at many places. Schezwan was not that spicy and I felt that something was missing.

3. Tandoor paneer pizza - So I tried it from the shop that was just next to the paani Puri shop. The pizza was of the thin crust base and I felt it was okayish. You can better try it from the pasta stall the one on the street.

4. Veg tikka : So at this tikka place you can get potatoes, tomatoes, mushroom and Shimla mirch tikka. I recommend you to try this for just Rs. 40 plate and you can experience good food here. The tikka is served with onion and green chutney. ❤️ Recommended

5. Pasta - We tried pink sauce penne pasta. It was definitely worth it. Tangy taste, good quantity and range is of 70-200 you shall visit this stall. You can choose your own pasta and the sauce.

After this we took a break as we wanted to explore more but our stomach started saying no, so we took one jaljeera soda from the stall just next to the tikka stall and went for a walk to see some nearby places. Then we came back with the bang. After the break we tried

6. Mysore dosa - So frankly speaking I like dosa crunchy but the one which they served was soggy and I feel that you can skip the dosa part here or at least the Mysore dosa you can skip. You can try some other better dosas.

7. Bellbottom shake : Last but not the least I'll definitely recommend you to try this. With the toppings of dry fruit, one scoop of vanilla, blue berry and thick shake of strawberry and blue berry. You will love it. I wanted to try this and I did not regret it.

You can also find Franky, sandwiches and other stalls. I only tried all this but there is much more variety. For Western line you just need to take a slow train and get down at Charni road station. Whereas for the central and harbour line people you need to get down at dadar and then you can take the churchgate slow train and get down at Charni road station.

featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Kasture
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bademiyan is one of Mumbai’s most iconic food spots, and it definitely lives up to its reputation. Located in Colaba, this place is especially famous for its late-night crowd and irresistible aroma of freshly grilled kebabs. The moment you arrive, you can see the energy—people waiting, food being prepared live, and the buzz of a true street food legend.

I tried the seekh kebabs, chicken tikka, and their signature rolls, and everything was cooked to perfection. The meat was juicy, well-marinated, and full of rich, smoky flavor. The rolls, in particular, are a must-have—perfectly wrapped, filling, and extremely satisfying. Portion sizes are decent, and the quality of ingredients stands out.

Service is quick despite the heavy rush, which is impressive. The staff is efficient and manages orders well, even during peak hours. Prices are slightly on the higher side compared to regular street vendors, but you’re paying for both taste and legacy.

Seating can be limited, and you might have to stand or wait, but that’s part of the authentic experience. Overall, Bademiyan is a must-visit for anyone who wants to enjoy classic Mumbai street-style Mughlai food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely disgusting and deeply disappointing experience at Bade Miyan.

I ordered a chicken biryani and was horrified to find a cockroach in it while eating. Finding a cockroach in food is a serious hygiene and food safety issue, and it completely ruined the meal and the entire dining experience.

What was even more disappointing was how the situation was handled. We immediately brought the matter to the attention of the owner/management, expecting an apology, an explanation, and some accountability. Instead, the bill was quietly deleted/cancelled, and it appeared that the management was more interested in making the issue disappear than addressing the underlying hygiene problem.

This is not just about one spoiled meal. It is about customer safety, cleanliness, and how a business responds when a serious issue is reported. I have photographs of the cockroach in the biryani and am sharing them along with this review.

A restaurant’s reputation means nothing if basic hygiene standards are not maintained. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this place and would urge potential customers to consider this incident before deciding to dine here.

We ordered soups that were clearly mentioned as “serves 2–3,” but the quantity wasn’t even sufficient for one person. The Chicken kebab was extremely plain, bland, and lacked even the most basic seasoning — it felt like zero effort went into preparing it.
The most disappointing item was the so-called paya soup, which felt like a newly invented disaster. It tasted like colorful water with no depth, richness, or authenticity whatsoever.
Overall, this place is living purely on past hype. Poor taste, misleading portion sizes, and unjustified pricing make this an experience I would never recommend. Definitely not worth the money or the wait.

customer_updates.name: SMRUTISIKHA PRADHAN
customer_updates.text:
• Cannon Pav Bhaji is one of Mumbai's most famous street food destinations, located opposite CSMT.
• Established in 1975 by a former Indian Army veteran, it has been serving Mumbaikars and travelers for decades.
• Known for its rich, buttery, and flavorful pav bhaji made in the traditional Mumbai style.
• The pav is perfectly toasted with butter and pairs wonderfully with the delicious bhaji.
• The place has a unique old-Mumbai charm and is an important part of the city's food heritage.
• Despite being a simple standing food stall, it attracts food lovers from across India.
• Quick service, authentic taste, and a nostalgic atmosphere make the experience memorable.
• A must-visit spot for anyone who wants to enjoy Mumbai's legendary pav bhaji and experience a piece of the city's culinary history.

Overall: Great taste, rich history, and a true Mumbai street-food experience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Pardeshi
featured_reviews.review_text: Canon Pav Bhaji did not live up to the hype at all. I have had much better pav bhaji at many other places. I ordered one Amul Butter Pav Bhaji and one Amul Butter Cheese Pav Bhaji. Both were extremely bland and lacked proper spices. There was an excessive amount of butter added, to the point that only butter’s taste was overpowering everything else—no real flavor of the bhaji could be felt. The pav bhaji was not even served properly hot, which made the experience worse. On top of that, the prices are very high for the quality and taste offered. This review is purely based on my personal experience, and unfortunately, it was very disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Cannon Pav Bhaji near CST and, unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing. We tried several items Pav Bhaji, Sheera, Sabudana Khichdi and Lassi and to be frank, everything was absolutely tasteless. For a place that is always crowded and located in such a prime spot, I genuinely expected much better in terms of flavour and quality.

The Pav Bhaji lacked the rich, buttery taste and balanced spices that you normally find even at simple street side stalls across Mumbai. The Sheera was bland and lacked the aroma and sweetness that make it enjoyable. Sabudana Khichdi, which is usually comforting and flavourful, felt underwhelming as well. Even the Lassi didn’t have the freshness or thickness you would hope for.

It feels like the only advantage this place has is its central location right outside CST, which naturally attracts tourists and daily commuters. In contrast, some of the other nearby stalls actually serve tastier food at far more economical prices.

Overall, Cannon Pav Bhaji didn’t live up to its hype or its location. If you’re looking for flavourful, satisfying Mumbai street food, you’re better off exploring the smaller stalls around the area.

featured_reviews.name: Vainateya Sahasrabudhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre in Mumbai my grandfather used to take me to have pav bhaji 2000 to 2014. Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a renowned destination for street food enthusiasts, serving mouth-watering pav bhaji that has captured the hearts of many. This iconic eatery has earned a reputation for its delicious food, prompt service, and cozy ambiance.

Ambiance
The ambiance at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is warm and inviting, perfect for a quick bite or a casual meal with friends and family. The decor is minimal, but the vibrant atmosphere and aroma of freshly cooked food make up for it.

Menu and Offerings
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's menu is centered around its signature dish, pav bhaji, which is a flavorful mix of vegetables cooked in a rich tomato-based gravy, served with soft, buttery pav bread. Some popular items on the menu include-
- *Pav Bhaji*: The star of the show, made with a medley of vegetables and spices, served with pav bread.
- *Special Pav Bhaji*: A variation of the classic dish, made with extra butter and spices.

Quality and Taste
The quality and taste of Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's offerings are exceptional. The pav bhaji is cooked to perfection, with a rich, buttery flavor that's hard to resist. Customers rave about the delicious food, and many have returned for years, making it a testament to the eatery's consistency.

Service
The service at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is prompt and efficient, ensuring that customers receive their orders quickly and without any hassle. The staff is friendly and courteous, adding to the overall positive experience.

Value for Money
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers excellent value for money, with prices starting from around ₹120-₹200 per person for a meal. Given the quality and quantity of food, it's a steal.

Tips
- Visit Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre during off-peak hours to avoid crowds.
- Try the special pav bhaji for an extra-rich flavor experience.
- Pair your pav bhaji with a buttermilk, lassi or cold drink for a refreshing contrast.

Online Ordering and Delivery
For those who prefer the convenience of home delivery, Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers online ordering through platforms like Justdial and Zomato. This allows customers to enjoy their favorite dishes from the comfort of their own homes.

Overall Experience
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience the best of Mumbai's street food scene. With its delicious pav bhaji, prompt service, and excellent value for money, it's a culinary gem that will leave you wanting more.

Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

Kheema Pav Review: Heaven‑Level Street Fix

This is the version you tell people about: hot keema—fine‑grain mutton, tomatoes, green chili—heaped on a plate with butter‑licked pav maska toasted till the edges crunch. Special Chai arrives in a huge glass, milky‑sweet with ginger bite, just enough to cut the fat. You break pav, drag it through keema, sip chai, repeat. It’s messy, fast, and perfect at 8 am when the stall lights flick on. You really do have to eat it there to get the story. 10/10, no substitutes.

The bun looked like a burger bun and had little nibs of colorful jelly mixed in. The people around us were eating proper bun maskas with pav and it seemed to me that we have perhaps been served a bastardized version intentionally to cater to our foreign palates. I asked the waiter if we can get the same dish as the other guests were eating, but English was obviously a problem and we have just received the bill and the waiter cleaned the table. I hope this was just a misunderstanding, but if you are a western tourist, eat elsewhere.

featured_reviews.name: Mallesh Mally
featured_reviews.review_text:
Before heading into the electric atmosphere of the MI vs SRH match, I made a pitstop at Raju Ki Chai, and it turned out to be a great decision.

The Vibe
The shop has a really good atmosphere. It’s clean and has all the facilities you’d want for a comfortable sit-down. It was the perfect place to soak in the pre-match excitement. Even though the stadium was already turning into a sea of blue flags, as an SRH fan, I felt totally at home here getting my caffeine fix.

The Taste
The most important part—the tea! I have to say, the taste was excellent. It’s a proper, well-brewed cup of chai that hits the spot. If you’re a tea lover like me, you’ll definitely appreciate the quality they’re serving.

The Value
I noticed that the prices are a little bit high compared to your average tea stall, but honestly, for the taste and the clean environment, it felt worth it. You get what you pay for, and in this case, it’s a premium experience.

We decided to sit and order Murgh seekh roll and Galauti Mutton kebab. Murgh seekh roll was very sad, dry and hard but Galauti mutton kebabs were too amazing and literally mouth-watering.
You can definitely visit this place to have the best kebab but before visiting just check once whether their AC is operational or not.

featured_reviews.name: Monal Saxena
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely terrible experience at Kabab Gunj, Colaba.

The food was extremely disappointing. The chicken was either not cooked properly or so badly overdone that it felt as hard as a stone. It was dry, tough, and completely unenjoyable. For a place serving kebabs, this is basic — and they failed at it.

The seekh kebab was even more shocking. It tasted exactly like a packaged, pre-cooked Zorabian seekh kebab — nothing fresh, nothing special, nothing that felt made in-house. It honestly felt like something taken out of a packet, reheated, and served. That’s not what you expect when you go out for kebabs.

The service was just as bad. There was only one staff member managing everything, and he was constantly running back and forth handling Zomato delivery orders. As dine-in customers, we were barely attended to. He kept coming and going, but we received no proper service or attention. I genuinely felt invisible sitting there.

Overall, a completely disappointing experience — poor food quality and worse service.

If you’re a true kebab lover like me, this is definitely not the place for you. Save your time and money and go somewhere that actually values its customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Pizza Dude Roman Style Pizza is one of my favorite places to visit after office hours. It’s a small and unique café with a cozy open seating setup, and that’s what makes the vibe feel so relaxing and peaceful. Since it’s just a 1-minute walking distance from Charni Road railway station, it becomes the perfect spot to grab a hot coffee and spend some quality time.

I always try their hot Americano, and last time I had it with their famous pesto sandwich — the taste was absolutely mind-blowing. They have many varieties of sandwiches and Roman-style pizzas, and everything feels fresh and full of flavor. They also serve brownies, which go perfectly with coffee.

The service is really good and the staff is friendly too. I sometimes go there after office just to relax, refresh my mind, and enjoy the calm atmosphere. It’s a perfect little hangout café with good food, good coffee, and a very comfortable vibe. Definitely one of those places you keep visiting again and again.

featured_reviews.name: shantam malgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Pizza Dude at Charni Road and this place is honestly a hidden gem. It’s located behind Saifee Hospital, opposite Hinduja College, and has a really cozy, quiet vibe — perfect if you want to escape the usual Mumbai chaos.

We tried the Ema Dashi Bhutan Special and Spicy Margherita, both made on their fresh sourdough base, and the texture was amazing — light, crispy, and full of flavour.

Also had the grilled veggies sandwich, which was easily a 10/10, along with a refreshing basil lemonade. Ended the meal with a chocolate mousse that was rich and super smooth.

If you enjoy sourdough pizzas and are looking for a low-key, cute spot in South Mumbai, this place is definitely worth checking out. Would highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Vijet Is Live
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Taste, Ready-Made Surprise
I recently visited Pizza Dude, looking forward to watching them craft a fresh pizza from scratch. However, I was a bit disappointed to find that they use pre-made, ready-to-bake pizza bases. Given the artisanal"dude" branding, I was expecting a live dough-tossing experience, making the base choice feel a bit underwhelming at first.
That said, I have to give credit where it's due—the taste was genuinely good! Despite the base not being freshly stretched in front of me, they managed to turn it into something quite tasty. The toppings were fresh, well-balanced, and the pizza was assembled and baked perfectly to a crispy finish The staff was friendly, and the overall, the flavor profiles they offer are strong. If you are looking for a quick, convenient, and tasty slice, it’s a good spot. However, if you are a stickler for authentic, freshly made-to-order sourdough crusts, you might feel a little disappointed with the base

Overall, it was a wonderful experience — great taste, friendly service, and definitely a place I’d love to visit again. Highly recommended for anyone craving delicious, authentic pizza in Mumbai!

featured_reviews.name: Divyansh Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I'm absolutely loving the Sev Khamani at Opera House Sev Khamani! Recently shifted near Red Church, this tiny shop packs a big punch. For just ₹25, you get a plateful of delicious, fulfilling Sev Khamani that's hard to resist. What sets it apart is the absence of spices, oil, or ghee, making it a great option for health-conscious foodies like me. During the monsoon season, their hot Sev Khamani is especially satisfying. Highly recommended!

*Update:* However, I did find that Opera House Sev Khamani has a different location listed online - Shop 19/B, Ajanta Shopping Center, Trikamdas Road, Malad West. If you're planning to visit, it's best to confirm the address before heading out.

featured_reviews.name: Akxhay kirpekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mag St. at Apollo Bandar is easily one of the most enjoyable casual dining spots in South Mumbai right now. The space has a very relaxed yet polished energy, the service team is genuinely warm and efficient, and the overall experience feels extremely well thought out from start to finish.

A big plus in this part of Mumbai is that valet parking is available, which makes visiting far more convenient than most places nearby.

The food quality was outstanding across the board, fresh ingredients, clean flavors, excellent execution, and portions that feel fair for the pricing. Nothing felt gimmicky or overdone. Just really good food made with consistency and confidence. The menu strikes a smart balance between comfort and creativity.

What stood out most was how appropriately priced everything felt for the quality, location, and overall dining experience. In a city where many places are either overpriced or underwhelming, Mag St. manages to deliver genuine value.

Definitely a place worth revisiting, whether for coffee, brunch, or a relaxed meal with friends. Apollo Bandar needed a place like this.

featured_reviews.name: Divya V. Naik
featured_reviews.review_text: Had the fried chicken sandwich, Korean cream cheese bun, and coffee – everything was absolutely amazing! The flavors were spot on, the food felt fresh, and the overall vibe of the place is great. Definitely worth visiting if you’re around Colaba.

featured_reviews.name: Dr.Saranya Sasi
featured_reviews.review_text: First-time visit, and I was totally impressed-everything was on point! The food was absolutely delicious, bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. The ambience was cozy yet stylish, with a thoughtfully designed interior that made the space feel both welcoming and upscale. The service was friendly, attentive, and quick, making the whole experience smooth and enjoyable. Overall, it’s a standout spot that’s perfect for a relaxed meal or catching up with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Anggie Puji
featured_reviews.review_text:
We actually found Mag St thanks to a girl we met at The Table who handed us a little Colaba guidebook and told us to eat like locals. So glad we followed her advice! We stopped in for an early dinner and tried the pizza and Asian fried rice – both were amazing. The fried rice really surprised us (and we’re Asian!), and the pizza was exactly my style: thin, cheesy, and so satisfying.

Didn’t get to try the bread yet, but it’s on the list for next time. Definitely a recommended stop in Colaba if you want great food with local vibes.

featured_reviews.name: Ayushi Sancheti
